title: ¿Cómo se llamaba?, tenía, tenía que, ayer; irregular: veía, era, iba

cards.title: tenía = I used to have
cards.body: Watch the small words too: una casa grande. Cuatro = four (think 'quarter').

examples.en: We used to have a big house.
I used to have four, but now I don't have any left.
examples.es: Tenía cuatro, pero ahora no me queda(n).

cards.title: tenía que = had to; ayer = yesterday
cards.body: The line past works for 'had to'. ¿No tenías que…? can mean 'weren't you supposed to…?'.

examples.en: I had to see you yesterday.
Weren't you supposed to do it yesterday?

cards.title: Only three irregulars: ver → veía
cards.body: This tense is very regular. Ver keeps the extra e, as in veo.

examples.en: I was seeing / we were seeing

cards.title: ser → era (think 'an era')
cards.body: A line in the past, like an era. The stress stays put: éramos.

examples.en: I used to be a student.

cards.title: ir → iba
cards.body: A blend of -aba and -ía. Iba a = 'was going to', and it takes a (movement); in fast speech the a's blend together.

examples.en: I was going to call you.
We were going to do them.

practice.en: We used to have a big house.
I had to see you (informal) yesterday.
Didn't you (informal) have to do it yesterday?
I used to be a student.
I was going to call you (informal).
I was going to do it.
